label: communicated to
definition: Argument 1 addressed, contacted or sent a message to argument 2.
scope_notes: Tell, ask, urge, warn, write, talk and message recipient paths establish directed communication. Accusing or describing another person without addressing them is not enough. Sending a person somewhere is not sending them a message.

facts.reason: Bush accuses or refers to Gore, but no row establishes a message addressed to Gore rather than a statement about him.
Clinton explicitly asks and tells Congress; these directly establish the communication recipient.
David practices in Manhattan and has an of-city/brother path; these are location or biographical evidence, not communication to a recipient.
Torre tells, speaks to and asks Williams, supporting communication in this direction.
The explicit tell path supports Bush communicating to Kerry, even though most other rows concern political rivalry or statements about Kerry.
